name: FAB
purpose: A floating, high-emphasis icon-only action fixed to a mobile viewport (typically 'add' / 'compose' / the one decisive action of a screen). PROPOSED #209 (itinerary row 7, slug fab) — NOT GATED, NOT RULED. An Icon-button idiom, per the wave-3 brief: PRIMARY tier tokens, B-D7 press-physics and the glyph-presence discipline are all copied verbatim from Icon-button.reference; what is NEW is the larger 56px target, the drop shadow (a floating control needs a depth cue Icon-button never needed, since Icon-button never floats above content), and a fixed mobile placement.

props.name: glyph
props.$note: Icon id from the assets/icons sprite; drives the accessible name unless aria-label overrides. Specimen uses global-controls/add.svg.

props.name: label
props.$note: REQUIRED accessible name (aria-label). Icon-only, same 4.1.2/2.4.4 requirement as Icon-button.

variants.name: primary
variants.use: The ONLY tier specimen'd. A FAB is by definition the single most decisive action available on a mobile screen — Icon-button's secondary/tertiary/quaternary tiers exist for lesser emphasis, which a FAB by convention never is. Whether a non-primary FAB should exist at all is named in decisionsForDave, not built.

tokens.target-size: ⚠ 56x56 — a PROPOSED RAW CONSTANT, NOT a store token (icon-scale.json tops out at icon.large=36px glyph; layout.json's target/min ladder tops out at 44px). Flagged in the snippet header and here; minting a fab/size token is Dave's call.
tokens.glyph-size: 24px = icon-scale.medium (the one token-bound dimension on this control)

primary.$note: Copied byte-for-byte from Icon-button.reference's primary tier — Mono monochrome, no red; hover renders as 0.70 opacity over the page.

tokens.elevation: elevation.functional (box-shadow) — the ONE token Icon-button never needed, because Icon-button never floats above page content.
tokens.radius: border-radius.control — flat/angular (B-D7), same as Icon-button. ⚠ Whether a FAB should DEVIATE from the angular rule (most systems that ship a FAB make it circular) is Dave's, flagged not taken — same class of question as Payment-card-visual's corner finding.
tokens.placement: 24px bottom/right offset (6 x 4px grid) — a raw constant, not a token (no z-index/offset token exists for floating chrome in the store).
tokens.$note: NO NEW TOKEN IS WANTED OR MINTED from the store's live rungs. --target and the 24px placement offset are the only non-token values, both declared raw constants, never silently invented as token names.

motion.hover: scale(1 + press-travel/56) — B-D7 pixel-true, size-scoped to the 56px target exactly as Icon-button scopes to 44px.
motion.reducedMotion: Transforms/brightness disabled under prefers-reduced-motion; the static colour states convey everything.

responsive.rule: Fixed viewport placement (bottom-right, 24px offset) on mobile; does not reflow with its container the way Button's action-bar does. Whether a FAB should reposition or hide on very small viewports / when a keyboard is open is unspecified — see decisionsForDave.

livesInside: Page (fixed overlay, not a layout child)
mustNotNeighbour: Back to top (both are fixed bottom-right floating controls; collision unresolved, see decisionsForDave)
commonPatterns: single decisive mobile action (add / compose / new)

accessibility.name: MANDATORY accessible name via aria-label — icon-only, no visible label (4.1.2 / 2.4.4), identical requirement to Icon-button.
accessibility.keyboard: Reachable in tab order; Enter/Space activate. Because it floats fixed to the viewport, its position in DOM/tab order relative to page content is a UX-writing decision not resolved here (typically placed last in source order).
accessibility.focus: Visible focus outline (text.default), never removed without replacement.
accessibility.target: 56x56 (exceeds the 44px floor deliberately — floating controls conventionally get a larger target since there is no neighbouring control to collide with).
accessibility.nonText: Glyph >=3:1 against its background (1.4.11); disabled glyph stays a visible ghost via text.on-disabled (B-D4), contrast-exempt but never invisible.

antiPatterns: A disabled (or any-state) glyph bound to a token equal to its own surface (glyph-presence gate, inherited from Icon-button).
Placing more than one FAB on the same screen (dilutes 'the one decisive action').
Hard-coding the 56px target or the 24px offset as though they were resolved store tokens — they are DECLARED raw constants pending Dave's mint-or-accept call.
REVIEW (inferred): using a FAB where the action already has an obvious home in the page header / toolbar (a FAB should be reserved for contexts where no such chrome exists, e.g. a full-bleed list).

tokenValidation.result: PROPOSED — worker lane render-verify only (light+dark, headless Chromium, 0 console errors). _validate_snippets.py / _validate_a11y.py / _validate_type_composites.py / _validate_grid.py / _validate_radius.py NOT RUN by this lane (conductor's serial set, per the wave-3 brief). This is a PROPOSAL, not a proof-of-done.
tokenValidation.$note: Not registered in component-types.json (shared file, outside this lane's fence). Not in _validate_radius.MIGRATED_SNIPPETS. No .cn-fab scope exists in canon.css. The 56px target is a DECLARED GAP against the token store, not a silent invention — see tokens.target-size.

$differsFrom.Icon-button: Same tokens, same tier discipline, same press-physics MODEL — but FAB floats fixed above page content (needs elevation.functional, a shadow Icon-button never binds), is larger (56 vs 44), and is placement-constrained (mobile viewport corner) rather than living inline in a toolbar/input/table row.

$decisionsForDave: Should the FAB deviate from the angular corner rule and render circular, the way most systems that ship a FAB do? Flagged, not taken.
Should a fab/size (56px) and a floating-chrome offset (24px) token be minted, or is 56/24 acceptable as house-standard raw constants forever?
FAB vs Back-to-top collision: both are fixed bottom-right. When a screen could show both, which wins the corner, or do they stack?
Is a non-primary-tier FAB ever legitimate, or is 'FAB = the one decisive primary action' a hard rule?

usedInContext.$note: Page (fixed overlay, not a layout child)

mustNotNeighbour.$note: Back to top (both are fixed bottom-right floating controls; collision unresolved, see decisionsForDave)
